queries.hook: I feel lonely. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Loneliness and emptiness come from feeling separate from people, purpose and the divine; the heart is searching for where it belongs.
queries.steady: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.
queries.act: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
hook.sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
hook.line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
hook.translation: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.

words.en: by the boat of knowledge alone

hook.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.
hook.misuse: Not 'understanding cancels the harm done to others'; it frees you to change and make amends.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Before his final words, Krishna tells Arjuna why he is saying them.
alternates.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
alternates.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
alternates.translation: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
alternates.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
alternates.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
alternates.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
alternates.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
alternates.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, convinced he is about to commit the worst sin by fighting his own kin. Krishna tells him that even if he were the most sinful of all sinners, the raft of knowledge would carry him across. The point is that learning with humility and trust can cut through the deepest doubt, freeing you to act without being crushed by guilt.
verse.for_you: You are studying and feeling cut off, convinced you do not belong. This verse says that even the worst wrongdoer is carried across by the raft of knowledge. Let that be the truth of your desk right now. You do not need to be perfect to learn.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind says you are not worthy and let the thought pass without agreeing with it.
verse.scene_line: You are on the battlefield of your own doubt, and the raft of knowledge is already there.
asks: What does the raft of knowledge feel like to me right now?
How do I let go of the guilt of feeling unseen?
What is one small thing I can learn without proving anything?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
verse.line: Where did this weakness come from, at the very moment it matters most?
verse.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Where has this faintness of heart come upon you in this crisis, Arjuna? It is not fitting for the noble, it does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
verse.misuse: Not shaming fear; it's the opening of a long, patient answer.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Krishna is looking at Arjuna, who has dropped his bow and sits in the middle of the battlefield, unable to move. He has just admitted that he is confused and does not know what is right. Krishna asks him where this weakness has come from at the moment it matters most. The verse says that this kind of faint-heartedness does not lead upward and brings disgrace. It is a call to admit that you do not know the way forward and to ask for guidance.
verse.for_you: You are sitting in your own study space, feeling the weight of being unseen among your friends and doubting your place in your classes. This faintness is not a sign that you are failing.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment you feel most unseen today.
verse.scene_line: You are on the battlefield of your own study, and you have dropped your bow.
asks: How do I ask for help without feeling like a burden?
What does it mean to admit I do not know the path?

verse.speaker: Surdas
verse.setting: Surdas asks to be kept in shelter.
verse.sanskrit: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥
verse.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
verse.translation: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
verse.meaning: Surdas speaks to the Lord from a place of being overwhelmed. He says that he was being swept away, but by grace, elders were sent to catch his hand and save him. The verse proposes that even when you are drowning in your own doubts and feelings of unworthiness, grace finds a way to send someone to steady you. You do not have to pull yourself out alone.
verse.for_you: You are in the library or the hostel, and the distance between you and the friends you thought you had feels like a wide river you cannot cross. You feel unseen in the middle of the room.
verse.try_today: Notice the small act of care from a friend or teacher today.
verse.scene_line: You are being swept away, and someone is sent to catch your hand.
asks: How do I know when grace is reaching for me?
Can I trust a hand I do not expect to hold?
What does it mean to be caught rather than to save myself?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verse.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
verse.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.

words.en: becoming one with the supreme reality

verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna about the person who is truly wise. This person finds their happiness inside, not in the world around them. Their joy does not depend on what happens to them. They are not lifted up by success or brought down by failure. They see that pleasure from the senses is temporary. It starts and it ends. Because they understand this, they do not chase after it. They find a steady light within themselves. This inner light is their guide. It helps them stay calm and free.
verse.for_you: The doubt and the loneliness you feel are not the whole truth. They are just weather passing through. There is a steadiness inside you that does not depend on anyone else seeing you. You can rest in that quiet place, even when the room feels empty.
verse.try_today: Find one small moment of quiet and sit with it.
verse.scene_line: You are in a quiet room, looking for a light that does not flicker with the day's noise.
asks: How do I find this light when everything feels so heavy?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verse.sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
verse.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verse.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is telling Rama that four qualities guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He says you do not need to master all of them at once. You only need to choose one. If you start with good company, the others will grow around it. The verse says that even when you are at your lowest and most helpless, you could hold on to good company and not let it go.
verse.for_you: You have been sitting with this feeling of being cut off, as if the space between you and your friends is a wall you built yourself. But the texts say that at your lowest, you do not need to fix the whole room.
verse.try_today: Send a message to one person you trust, and ask them to meet you without a plan.
verse.scene_line: You are at the lowest point, and the gatekeeper of good company is still there, waiting.
asks: How do I ask for company without sounding needy?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The Isha on seeing one life in all beings.
verse.sanskrit: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥
verse.line: See yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, and you stop recoiling from people.
verse.translation: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, no longer shrinks away from anyone.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.meaning: The seer speaks to the one reading, after the Isha has said that all of life belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. The seer says that if you see all beings in your own self, and your own self in all beings, you will no longer shrink away from anyone.
verse.for_you: You feel cut off from the people around you. The Isha asks you to stop shrinking. If you can see your own face in theirs, the distance will not feel so hard to cross.
verse.try_today: Notice one detail about a friend that you share.
verse.scene_line: You are standing in a room full of people, and you see yourself in all of them.
asks: How do I see myself in people who feel far away?
Can I enjoy being with others without holding on?

story.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
story.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
story.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
story.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

anchor.speaker: Bhasa
anchor.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
anchor.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
anchor.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
anchor.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
anchor.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

story.hook_title: Two childhood friends met again as old men, and neither had found peace
story.teaser: Two childhood friends met again as old men, and neither had found peace
story.for_you: Bhasa and Vilasa spent a lifetime proving their worth through effort, only to find themselves alone at the end. You are in a similar stretch, where the lists of what you could do to be enough keep spinning.
asks: How do I stop the list from owning my quiet moments?
What if I am enough before the next exam or task?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: the first being, alone.
verse.sanskrit: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
verse.translation: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

verse.meaning: In the beginning, one being existed alone. He felt fear. He asked himself why. Since there was nothing else, there was no second to threaten him. His fear left him. Fear comes from the presence of another. Joy came later, when he split into two to keep him company.
verse.for_you: You are in a room with people but you feel like the only one there. The distance between you and your friends is real, even if no one has said a word. You are not wrong to feel this way. The fear is not a weakness.
verse.scene_line: You are the first being, alone in a room full of people, and you feel the fear of a second who is not there.
asks: What am I afraid of when I am alone in a crowd?
How do I find a real connection when the distance feels so wide?
Can I stand in this feeling without shrinking?

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.meaning: The sage Ashma tells King Janaka that the mind suffers only from two things. One is something unwanted happening to you. The other is a mind that spins and wanders, making trouble out of nothing. There is no other source of mental pain. The mind then asks what you are, and you steady yourself on the people still sitting in front of you.
verse.for_you: That unease in the study hall, the silence between texts, is the mind spinning. You are not cut off, but the mind is making a room where no one is. The people still in front of you are your next step.
verse.try_today: Name the one thing your mind is spinning about right now.
verse.scene_line: You are the king, and the sage asks who you are when the noise stops.
asks: How do I know when my mind is just spinning?
How do I steady myself on people when I feel so alone?

verse.speaker: Surdas
verse.setting: Surdas on belonging that does not depend on being good.
verse.sanskrit: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥
verse.line: Good or bad, we are still yours.
verse.translation: Good or bad, we are yours. Our shame and our honour are yours to carry. Hear my plea, my Lord.
verse.why: Our shame is not ours to carry alone.

matched.label: I feel ashamed of who I am

verse.meaning: Surdas, a poet who was blind, speaks to the Lord. He says that whether a person does good things or bad things, they belong to God. Their shame and their honour belong to God to carry. The verse means that the weight of who we are is not ours to carry alone.
verse.for_you: The quiet in the library and the doubt that you do not belong are heavy. You do not have to carry the weight of being worthy alone. There is a belonging that is already given, not earned. Let that be the ground you stand on.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you feel unseen and let the idea of belonging settle there.

verse.speaker: Rahim
verse.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
verse.sanskrit: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
verse.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verse.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
verse.meaning: Rahim is speaking to someone who feels the need to explain their inner life to the world. They are living in a love so close it needs no news, a connection so intimate that every joy and every sorrow is already known. Nothing needs explaining. The verse proposes that the one who has made a home in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verse.for_you: You have been trying to explain your loneliness to your friends as if it is a problem they can fix. But the feeling of being cut off does not need to be translated for them. The distance you feel is not a failure of communication.
verse.try_today: Stop explaining your feelings to anyone today.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in a room full of friends, holding a silence that already knows its own shape.
asks: Why do I feel the need to explain what I feel?
Can I let the silence know its own shape?
What would change if I stopped explaining?

verse.speaker: Savitri
verse.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verse.sanskrit: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं / ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते / न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण संगतं / ततः सतां संनिवसेत्समागमे
verse.line: Even one meeting with a good person is a gift. Time with good people is never wasted.
verse.translation: Even one meeting with good people is something to wish for; friendship with them is better still. Time with a good person is never wasted, so live among the good.
verse.why: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

prasang.title: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.
prasang.story_hook: Savitri knew the exact day her husband would die, and she went into the forest with him anyway.
prasang.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

verse.meaning: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan. She does not beg or cry. She speaks with steady love and clear words about what is good and right. She says that even one meeting with a good person is a gift, and time with them is never wasted. She tells him to live among good people. Her determination carries her through what fear would drop. She does not fight him with force, but with truth.
verse.for_you: You have been waiting for the others to notice you, to close the distance. But the distance is not just theirs. It grows because you are not yet among the good you wish to be. You are in the study, but you are not yet with the good.
verse.try_today: Find one person in your class and ask them a real question about what they are studying.
verse.scene_line: You are walking behind your own fear, asking it what is real.
asks: How do I know if someone is good for me to be with?
What if I speak clearly but no one listens to me?
How do I stop feeling like an imposter when I am alone?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

matched.label: I feel ashamed of who I am

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the mind is the battlefield. When you are alone, you are not helpless. You can choose to be your own ally instead of your own tormentor. The self is the only tool you could lift itself up. It can also be the weight that pulls you down. There is no outside force stopping you. The choice is entirely in how you speak to yourself.
verse.for_you: You have felt cut off from the friends around you. The distance grew quietly. Now you sit with your books and feel like an imposter. But the self is the only friend you can truly count on in this room.
verse.try_today: When the feeling of loneliness rises, say one true thing to yourself that you would say to a friend.
verse.scene_line: You are the one who must lift yourself by your own hand.
asks: How do I know when my mind is my enemy?
What is one true thing I can say to myself?
How do I stop feeling like an imposter?

story.title: Sita in captivity
story.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.
story.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
story.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

anchor.speaker: Sita
anchor.setting: Alone in captivity, Sita fears Ram has forgotten her, then reassures herself.
anchor.sanskrit: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥
anchor.line: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is true only of the ungrateful. Real love survives distance.
anchor.translation: Love lasts while someone is in sight; out of sight, affection fades. But that is the way of the ungrateful. Ram will not let it fade.
anchor.why: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

prasang.title: Sita in captivity
prasang.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
prasang.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.
prasang.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

story.hook_title: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
story.teaser: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
story.for_you: You have been sitting with this feeling of being an imposter and feeling cut off from your friends. Sita was surrounded by people who mocked her and kept her lonely. She worried Ram had forgotten her. But she held on to the truth that real love survives distance.
asks: How do I know if the distance is real or only in my head?
What does it mean to hold on when I feel so alone?
How do I stop waiting for them to see me?

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call feeling cut off, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: Even among people, you've felt unseen, and the distance has grown without anyone saying so.

queries.hook: I feel lonely. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Loneliness and emptiness come from feeling separate from people, purpose and the divine; the heart is searching for where it belongs.
queries.steady: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.
queries.act: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.
queries.story: A story of a husband and wife, facing feeling cut off.

understanding.life_context: Studying. Feels uneasy; closest to "I feel lonely" and "I feel like an imposter".

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
verse.sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
verse.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
verse.translation: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.

words.en: standing in the heart of all beings

verse.why: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

prasang.title: Krishna describes his glories
prasang.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasang.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

verse.meaning: Krishna is listing the chief glories where the divine shows itself. He tells Arjuna that any excellence you see in the world is a spark of his splendour. The verse proposes that the self you feel cut off from is already seated in every heart, including your own. You do not need to find it by striving. It is the beginning, the middle and the end of every being, right now.
verse.for_you: You are studying in a room full of people, yet you feel like an imposter because you believe you could earn the right to be there. This verse says you do not have to earn it.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you did well today without needing praise for it.
verse.scene_line: You are in a crowded study hall feeling like a shadow, but the self is already seated in your heart.
asks: How do I feel the self when I feel so alone?
Why does being around people not make me feel less like an imposter?
How do I know the self is in me if I feel cut off?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verse.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verse.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
verse.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free. Ashtavakra answers that you are not your body or your roles, but the awareness that watches them. He says that if you believe you are free, you are free. If you believe you are bound, you are bound. The way you see yourself is what creates your reality.
verse.for_you: The doubt you carry about your place in the room is a belief, not a fact. This week has started to show you that your worth is not earned by a test score or a friend's text.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you feel unseen, and name it as a thought, not a truth.
verse.scene_line: You are the awareness watching the room, not the role you fear you play.
asks: How do I stop the doubt from defining me?
Can I choose a different story about myself?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verse.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verse.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
verse.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
verse.why: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

matched.label: I feel ashamed of who I am

prasang.title: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the self is like the sky. The sky is everywhere, but it is not stained by the clouds, the birds, or the storms that move through it. In the same way, the self is present in every body, but it is not stained by what happens to that body. The idea is simple. The self is a witness. It watches the actions and the feelings, but it does not take the marks of them. If you see that same presence in everyone else, you stop wounding yourself.
verse.for_you: You are sitting in your study, looking at your friends, and you feel the distance between you. You think they see something you do not have, and that thought is the stain. But the self is the same sky in them that it is in you.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the same room, but you see two skies looking at each other without touching.
asks: How do I tell the cloud from the sky?
Can I feel the self without stopping the study?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: One of the best-known verses of the Upanishad, on the God within all.
verse.sanskrit: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥
verse.line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
verse.translation: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
verse.why: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

prasang.title: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge
prasang.summary: Seekers ask what causes the world and governs their joys and sorrows. Through meditation they come to see one Lord, Rudra-Shiva, hidden in every heart; the Upanishad moves from inquiry to recognition to a prayer of refuge (6.18) and ends on grace and love of God (6.21, 6.23).
prasang.lesson: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

verse.meaning: The seer is speaking to the seekers who have asked what governs their joys and sorrows. They have looked outward and felt the weight of the world. Now the seer tells them that one God is hidden in every being, the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do. This means that the part of you that watches your thoughts and your loneliness is not the same as the thoughts. It is untouched by the noise of exams or the fear of not belonging. It simply sees.
verse.for_you: You are sitting in the library or your room, and the feeling of being an imposter is loud. The verse tells you that the part of you that notices this feeling is the same quiet witness that is in everyone. It is not judging.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment you feel most alone, and just watch it without naming it.
verse.scene_line: You are the quiet witness seated in your own heart, watching the crowd move through without touching you.
asks: How can I rest in a witness that does not fix anything?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
verse.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
verse.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.meaning: The seer speaks to the reader about how to live in the world. They say you could do your work and hope to live a full hundred years. The point is that if you do your work with a certain spirit, your actions will not stick to you. You hold what you have lightly, you keep going, and you see yourself in everyone you meet.
verse.for_you: You are studying and feeling cut off, as if the people around you are moving through a room you are not in. The verse says to do your work and wish for a hundred years, not to stop trying, but to do it without letting it own you.
verse.try_today: Do one small study task and then step away without checking for a reply.
verse.scene_line: You are at your desk, doing the work, and the distance is the space you keep.
asks: How do I do my work without letting it own me?
How do I see myself in others when I feel alone?

verse.speaker: Surdas
verse.sanskrit: कबहूँ तुम नाहिन गहरु कियो | सदा सुभाव-सुलभ सुमिरन-बस, भक्तनि अमर दियौ ॥
verse.line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.
verse.translation: You have never once delayed. By nature easy to reach and won over by remembrance, you have always given your devotees what is undying.
verse.meaning: Surdas speaks to the Lord, saying that the Lord has never delayed in answering. The Lord is naturally easy to reach, and simply by remembering him, one can win his grace. In this way, the Lord always gives his devotees what lasts forever.
verse.for_you: The distance you feel is not because anyone turned away, but because you are waiting for a sign that never arrives. The texts say that the Lord is already easy to reach. You do not need to prove your worth to be seen.
verse.try_today: Write one true thing about yourself and leave it where you will see it again.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of a room, waiting for someone to call your name, but the Lord is already easy to reach.
asks: How do I know when I am truly seen?
Can I be worthy without anyone else knowing?

story.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
story.story_hook: Among all the guards, one of them wiped Sita's tears and told her the truth.
story.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
story.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

anchor.speaker: Sita
anchor.setting: A kind guard, Sarama, offers to spy for Sita; Sita asks only to know what is decided about her.
anchor.sanskrit: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्। निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद्वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥
anchor.line: Whatever has been decided, just tell me. Not knowing is the hardest part.
anchor.translation: If there is any talk about him, or anything decided at all, tell me everything. That would be the greatest kindness to me.
anchor.why: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

prasang.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
prasang.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
prasang.story_hook: Among all the guards, one of them wiped Sita's tears and told her the truth.
prasang.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

story.hook_title: Among all of Sita's guards, one wiped her tears and told her the truth
story.teaser: Among all of Sita's guards, one wiped her tears and told her the truth
story.for_you: In your own place of study, a friend offered a quiet truth. That is what you need right now. The silence between you is not a wall, but a space waiting for a single honest word. Let the knowing come first, before the knowing becomes a burden you carry alone.
asks: What is one small truth I can share with a friend today?
How do I tell the difference between silence and safety?
